scientific_question: Does genetic-template adaptation in supplied liposomes plus abiotic polymer-vesicle production amount to one unassisted genome-and-compartment lineage with inherited function?

sources.authors: Abil, Restrepo Sierra, Stan et al.
sources.kind: experimental DNA replication/adaptation in synthetic liposomes
sources.audit_grade: E2-depth original main Results/Methods/Figures/Discussion; not E3 independent replication
sources.rights: Main article CC BY 4.0 with third-party exceptions; supplementary/raw data not independently audited
sources.founders: Three intermittent campaign histories, one semi-continuous campaign, one bulk control; rounds and assay wells not independent founders
positive: DNA encoding Phi29 polymerase and terminal protein sustained molecular replication in supplied PURE/liposomes
Int-WT(1) at least fivefold in-liposome amplification gain over 12 rounds
Reconstructed S79G and A80T have assay-dependent replication benefit
Semi-continuous full-length template persisted at least five cycles
negative: Int-WT(2) had no corresponding replication improvement
Int-Mut NGS suggests contamination and F62Y reversion
No-liposome bulk control lost full-length template by round six
Purified mutant polymerase did not improve bulk enzyme replication
interventions: PCR extraction and replenished liposomes in intermittent regime
Premanufactured lipid feeding vesicles and forced freeze-thaw every semi-continuous round
PURE translation proteins and external chemical substrates
confounds: Different 10x/100x bulk versus liposome dilution (authors report supplementary controls, not reanalyzed)
About half of DNA released on freeze-thaw; external DNA amplification possible

sources.kind: physical reproduction of polymer vesicles without genetically coded evolution
sources.audit_grade: E2-depth publisher main Results/Discussion/Methods summary; not supplements or data reanalysis
sources.rights: Main PNAS article CC BY 4.0; supplementary/third-party rights not audited
sources.founders: Three population time-series experiments on distinct dates with common chemical stocks; not independently evolved genotypes
positive: 0.22-micrometer retentate enriched for preexisting vesicles grew under 12h light, filtrate had no visible new vesicles
Reported parent-associated generation of later polymer vesicles under illuminated batch chemistry
94% of newly seen vesicles positive for inherited ZnTPP catalyst
negative: No new vesicles detected in the filtrate under corresponding illumination
Finite monomer supply changes growth dynamics
No experiment demonstrating a selectable, stable encoded genotype across pedigreed generations
interventions: Author-selected initial polymer precursors, photocatalyst and reaction architecture
Externally controlled green illumination and temperature
Filtration separation to distinguish population sources
confounds: Filtrate also deprived of ZnTPP catalyst, making negative filtrate result not purely ancestry specific
No individually tracked parent-child multi-generation failure denominators in main text
Main text lacks source-data-level independent audit of proposed membrane ejection and variation

independence: Separate author groups and distinct chemical systems, not direct independent replications of coupled genomic-and-compartment autonomous reproduction.
conclusion: Complementary functional components shown, but a single self-maintaining, independently reproducing genome-plus-compartment lineage with inherited adaptive benefit is not established by these original studies.

future_only_hypotheses.target: Lineage-resolved genotype-compartment transfer without membrane rebuilding or DNA rescue
Catalyst, polymer structural identity and causal inherited daughter-lineage fitness
Coupled self-maintaining template plus physical daughter vesicle without externally timed transfer
